title: Aurum Alpha health and readiness responses
description: Response shapes for /healthz and /readyz. Governed by standards/service.md SC1 and SC5. schemaVersion 1 — evolves additively per PC6.

status.description: The body's answer (SC1). Routing stays binary — 200 for ok and degraded, 503 for fail — because a load balancer has two behaviours; degraded exists so a human and a dashboard can see that something the service tolerates is broken.

checkStatus.description: One probe either worked or did not. Degradation is a property of the whole service, derived from which checks failed and whether they were required.

provenance.description: Which build this running process is (SC5). The same values appear in the startup log line.

service.description: The service's stable name, identical to the log line's service field.

version.description: The repository version this build was cut from, per the CI standard.

commit.description: Full 40-character git commit SHA — never abbreviated, so it is unambiguous to look up.

check.description: One dependency probe performed by /readyz (SC1). A readiness response that reports ok while checking nothing converts an unknown into a wrong answer.

required.description: Whether the service can serve traffic without this dependency (SC1, SC6). Declared per check rather than defaulted, because someone has to decide: a required check failing is 503, an optional one failing is degraded and still 200.

latency_ms.description: How long the probe took. A check that passes slowly is the earliest warning of one that will fail.

detail.description: Why a failing check failed. Present when status is fail; never carries a secret or a connection string.

livenessResponse.description: GET /healthz — 200 whenever the process is alive. Checks nothing (SC1) and carries provenance (SC5).

readinessResponse.description: GET /readyz — 200 with status ok or degraded, 503 with status fail when a required check fails (SC1). A misconfigured service reports fail here with a check named for its configuration and stays up rather than exiting (SC3, SC6).

checks.description: At least one: a service with no dependencies to check does not need a readiness endpoint distinct from liveness, and one that has them must probe them. A service blocked on its own configuration reports that as a check here.
